battle.name: 蘇瓦松戰役 (486年)
battle.theater: 法蘭西北部索瓦松平原
battle.brief: 486年，法蘭克王克洛維斯在索瓦松附近的瓦迪斯科斯原野，擊敗以羅馬人自居的索瓦松王國統治者西亞格里烏斯。此役把北高盧最後的羅馬式政權連同稅收與城防併入法蘭克王國，奠定墨洛溫王朝的霸業。雙方作戰早已不用亞述式複合長弓，靠的是日耳曼長矛、飛斧與大盾，亞述長弓只存於譜系之中。

kit.name: 亞述長弓
kit.history: 亞述人靠弓和鐵的組合征服兩河流域。弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。

countries: 索瓦松之戰的交戰方有兩支。甲方是薩利安法蘭克人，即活動於今法國北部與比利時南部的日耳曼部族聯盟；「薩利安」一名常被解釋為與某種兵器或佩帶的戰帶有關，語源至今仍無定論。這個聯盟以王為核心，周圍是一批立誓效忠的武裝隨從，族眾按氏族與地域集結，許多分隊是步騎合編的部落兵，武器自備，臨陣徵發。乙方是所謂索瓦松王國：西亞格里烏斯以羅馬人的名義佔有北高盧的殘餘，保留羅馬式稅制、法院程序與以自己名號鑄造的錢幣，靠貝利卡・塞昆達總督區各城的稅收維持一支羅馬正規軍殘部與高盧徵召兵，北方邊境另倚賴高日耳曼與東哥特盟軍。他承認東羅馬皇帝為宗主，卻從未獲得帝國正式冊封；格里高利・德・圖爾仍稱他為「羅馬人的王」，而他控制的土地不過是北高盧數個河谷與其城鎮。
countriesEn: The two sides at the Battle of Soissons were the Salian Franks on one hand and the so-called Kingdom of Soissons on the other. The Franks were a confederation of Germanic tribes operating in what is now northern France and southern Belgium; the name 'Salian' is often taken to refer to a particular weapon or to a war-belt worn at the waist, but its etymology remains unsettled. The confederation was organised around the king and a body of sworn war-companions, with the tribal levy gathered by clan and district, many units mixing foot and horse, bringing their own arms and mustering at the call of the war-leader. Their opponents, the Kingdom of Soissons, was the rump in northern Gaul over which Syagrius ruled in the name of the Romans: he kept the Roman tax system, Roman legal procedure and coins struck in his own name, and supported a remnant of the regular Roman army together with Gallic levies out of the revenues of the cities of the Belgica Secunda prefecture, while relying on High German and Ostrogothic allies for the northern frontier. He acknowledged the eastern emperor as his overlord but was never formally invested by the empire; Gregory of Tours still calls him 'king of the Romans', though the territory he actually held amounted to a few river valleys and their towns in northern Gaul.
people: 法蘭克方面的統帥是克洛維斯一世，名字在拉丁文作克洛多維庫斯，意思大約是「著名的戰士」。父王契得里克早年為羅馬效力，曾在皇帝康士坦提二世麾下作戰，與帝國訂有約定；克洛維斯於481年前後即位，五年之後在索瓦松與西亞格里烏斯交鋒。與他並肩的是出身王族與氏族首戶的武裝隨從，以及慣於在接觸前投擲飛斧的斧兵；卡西安多魯斯致東哥特王狄奧多里克的書信中提到法蘭克人「先拋出斧頭，然後才衝鋒」。格里高利記錄的克洛維斯騎著披甲駿馬、在潰退時仍率少數人回身再戰的形象，是這場戰役在後世記憶中最鮮明的一筆。索瓦松方面的主角是西亞格里烏斯，作為晚期羅馬官僚體系在北高盧的殘存代表而存在；有說他是將軍斯提利科親信的後裔，但無從證實。現存敘事主要出自格里高利・德・圖爾的《法蘭克人歷史》，該書寫成於戰役之後約八十年，帶有教會護教的立場。教會傳統把克洛維斯的勝利歸於王后克洛蒂爾德與聖雷米吉約斯的代禱，並以王后的信仰作為皈依天主教的背景。格里高利另記下「荊棘王冠」一段：一名士兵自灌木摘下金色荊棘冠替克洛維斯戴上並高呼「萬歲王」，克洛維斯此後戴它而不戴金冠。
peopleEn: On the Frankish side the commander was Clovis I, whose Latin name Chlodovicus means roughly 'famous warrior'. His father Childeric had long served Rome, fighting under Constantius II and entering into arrangements with the empire; Clovis had come to the throne around 481 and five years later met Syagrius near Soissons. Beside him stood war-companions drawn from the royal house and the leading clans, together with axe-men accustomed to hurling their weapons before contact; in a letter to the Ostrogothic king Theodoric, Cassiodorus records that the Franks 'throw the axe first and then charge'. Gregory of Tours' image of Clovis on his armoured horse, turning back with a handful of men while the rest gave way, is the most vivid stroke left in later memory of the battle. Syagrius, the principal figure on the Soissonian side, existed as the residual representative of the late Roman bureaucratic order in northern Gaul; the claim that he descended from the household of the general Stilicho cannot be substantiated. The surviving narrative comes mainly from Gregory of Tours' Histories of the Franks, written roughly eighty years after the battle and coloured by a churchly, providential standpoint. Church tradition attributed Clovis' victory to the prayers of his wife Clotilde and of Saint Remigius, and used the queen's faith as the background to his conversion. Gregory also preserves the story of the 'crown of thorns': a soldier picked a golden crown of thorns from a bush, set it on Clovis' head and shouted 'long live the king'; Clovis wore it thereafter in place of a golden crown.
kits: 亞述長弓是這張卡牌的裝備，但必須說清楚：486年的索瓦松原野上，沒有任何一方使用亞述式複合長弓。亞述長弓成形於西元前一千年前後，是把角、獸筋與木料層合成形的短而強的反曲弓，弦安在弓腹，長度約一公尺上下，配約六十至七十公分的箭，箭頭為青銅或鐵的三棱鏃；亞述軍隊把它架在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路，弓與鐵同時出現，是兩河流域被征服的關鍵。這種弓型在西元前七百年前後隨波斯與草原民族一路西傳，在西歐留下的最後痕跡是第四、五世紀的匈奴式複合弓與薩珊、拜占庭的弓兵傳統，到五世紀末在法蘭克與高盧一帶已斷了線索。索瓦松戰役真正在場的兵器是另一套：法蘭克人用日耳曼式長矛、闊刃短刀與長逾半公尺的橢圓形大盾，突擊單位以飛斧開路；格里高利描述法蘭克人戴著護顏的頭盔，護甲則由鎖子甲過渡到魚鱗甲的雙層結構。索瓦松的羅馬軍保留晚期帝國的裝備樣式：橢圓或圓形盾牌、分節鎧甲的殘餘、盔頂加護鼻的頭盔，以及人數銳減、退居二線的弓手編制。
kitsEn: The Assyrian bow is the piece of equipment on this card, but it must be stated plainly: on the plain of Soissons in 486 no side whatsoever used the Assyrian-type composite bow. The Assyrian bow was developed around the first millennium BC: a short, powerful recurved bow laminated from horn, sinew and wood, strung on the belly, around a metre in length, fired with arrows of roughly sixty to seventy centimetres tipped with bronze or iron trilobate points. The Assyrian army shot from the platform of the war chariot, the charioteers relying on the archers to open the way; bow and iron together were the key to the conquest of Mesopotamia. The type spread westward with Persian and steppe peoples from around the eighth century BC, and its last traces in western Europe are the Hunnic composite bows of the fourth and fifth centuries and the archery traditions of the Sasanian and Byzantine east; by the late fifth century the thread had broken off among the Franks and in Gaul. The weapons actually present at Soissons belonged to a different kit. The Franks used Germanic spears, broad-bladed short swords and oval shields over half a metre long, with assault units opening the way with throwing axes; Gregory describes Frankish helmets with cheek-guards and armour in the transition from mail to a double layer of scale. The Roman force at Soissons kept the late imperial style: oval or round shields, survivals of segmented armour, helmets with a reinforced brow, and a greatly reduced body of archers pushed into a secondary role.
tactics: 索瓦松一帶是一片開闊的播種平原，夾在艾納河的彎道與城郊沼澤之間；羅馬城踞高處，憑城牆與塔樓自守，因此交鋒必然發生在城外曠野，攻城與野戰的取捨立刻分曉。索瓦松方倚靠晚期帝國的防禦傳統：步兵排成密集縱隊與縱深方陣，中央由重裝盾兵支撐，騎兵置於兩翼，弓手與投射兵在側翼放箭，最後以精銳的步騎衝鋒制勝；這套做法在西元四、五世紀已因兵員下降而鬆散。西亞格里烏斯的軍隊多由城鎮民兵與羅馬殘兵組成，紀律與配合尚可，士氣與裝備則一路下滑。法蘭克方走相反路線：他們不打攻城戰，靠的是快速集結、騎兵衝鋒與步騎混編的散線，在平原上以速度換取縱深。卡西安多魯斯的書信提到法蘭克人慣於先拋擲戰斧再發動衝鋒，飛斧用來在接觸前削弱敵陣，近身之後靠大盾護身、長矛戳刺。格里高利寫到法蘭克人一度被追，但克洛維斯帶著少數人回身再戰，扭轉了局勢。整場戰鬥很可能只是幾個時辰的遭遇戰：沒有攻城，沒有長圍，勝負在平原上一個上午之內決定。後勤上，法蘭克人靠劫掠與徵發供給，羅馬方則靠城外莊園與稅收支撐遠征。
tacticsEn: The ground around Soissons is an open arable plain, hemmed in by the bend of the Aisne and the marshes outside the town; the Roman city stands on high ground and defends itself with ramparts and towers, so the clash could only take place in the open field beyond the walls, and the choice between siege and open battle was settled at once. The Soissonian side relied on the late imperial defensive tradition: infantry drawn up in dense columns and in depth, the centre braced by heavily shielded troops, cavalry on the wings, archers and missile troops shooting from the flanks, and a final decisive push by picked foot and horse. In the fourth and fifth centuries this had already loosened through the decline in manpower. Syagrius' army was largely drawn from the towns and from the Roman remnant: fair discipline and coordination, but worn-down morale and equipment. The Franks took the opposite road: no siege warfare, but rapid concentration, a cavalry charge and a loose line of combined foot and horse, trading depth for speed on the plain. Cassiodorus' letter notes the Frankish habit of throwing the axe first and then charging, the axes used to disorder the enemy before contact, followed by shield cover and the thrust of the spear. Gregory writes that the Franks were driven back for a while, until Clovis turned with a few men and reversed the business. The whole engagement was probably little more than a morning's clash of a few hours: no siege, no siege-lines, the result settled on a single field before midday. In logistics the Franks lived off plunder and requisition, while the Roman side supported its expedition from the manors and taxes of the countryside.
data: 關於蘇瓦松之戰，幾乎所有數字都不可靠，而這本身就是重要事實。格里高利・德・圖爾是現存唯一的同期敘述者，他沒有記下任何一方的人數；後世中世紀編年史把法蘭克人寫成數萬大軍，把索瓦松的軍隊寫得更小，這種量級屬於文學加工，而非史料。可以確定的是：戰役發生於西元486年，一般繫於9月27日；克洛維斯約自481年前後即位，此役在他的統治中期。唯一有依據的數字來自更早的協議：405年羅馬將軍斯提利科與法蘭克首領契得里克議定，法蘭克人定居在後來薩利安法典所稱的「薩利安之地」，並每年向羅馬進貢四千五百第納里，視為居留該地的租金，這筆錢一直付到西亞格里烏斯覆亡前後。領土與行程方面，索瓦松是貝利卡・塞昆達總督區的首府，該區在晚羅馬行政文獻中列有九座城邦，涵蓋皮卡第與瓦茲河一帶；克洛維斯的根據地在土爾奈與萊茵河下游之間，到索瓦松的直線行程約一百四十至一百五十公里，一次春季出擊即可抵達。索瓦松的晚期城牆環城約三點二公里，設塔樓四十餘座，是當時北高盧少數仍能長期據守的設防城市；而索瓦松盆地正是塞納—馬恩河下游最肥沃的農業區，爭奪它等於爭奪高盧北部的稅基。
dataEn: Almost every figure for the Battle of Soissons is unreliable, and that is itself an important fact. Gregory of Tours is the only contemporary narrative and he records no numbers for either side; later medieval chroniclers turned the Franks into an army of tens of thousands and the Soissonian force into something smaller, which is literary embellishment rather than evidence. What can be established is this: the battle was fought in AD 486, usually dated to 27 September; Clovis had taken the throne around 481, so the campaign falls in the middle of his reign. The only figure with a documentary basis comes from an earlier agreement: in 405 the Roman general Stilicho and the Frankish leader Childeric settled that the Franks would settle on land in what the later Salic law calls the 'Salic land', paying Rome 4,500 denarii a year as the rent of their residence, and that payment continued until around the fall of Syagrius. As for territory and distance, Soissons was the capital of the prefecture of Belgica Secunda, which late Roman administrative documents list as containing nine civitates covering Picardy and the valley of the Oise. Clovis' base lay between Tournai and the lower Rhine, roughly a hundred and forty to a hundred and fifty kilometres in a straight line from Soissons, within reach of a single spring campaign. The late Roman walls of Soissons enclosed some 3.2 kilometres with more than forty towers, making the town one of the few strongholds in northern Gaul still capable of a long stand; and the Soissonnais basin was the most fertile farmland of the lower Seine and Marne, so the struggle for it was a struggle for the tax base of northern Gaul.
cause: 蘇瓦松之戰的直接起因，是高盧北部最後一個羅馬式政權與法蘭克聯盟之間的生存競爭。背景要回到西元四世紀末的帝國崩解：406年，法蘭克人與其他日耳曼部族大批渡過萊茵河進入高盧；405年，羅馬將軍斯提利科以「土地租金」的名義把比利時境內一片地盤讓給法蘭克人，讓他們以同盟者身份替帝國守邊，並約束他們不得越界劫掠。這份協議維持數十年，但羅馬在北高盧的權力愈來愈空，稅收與徵兵的地基被各部族聯盟一塊塊切走；到五世紀中葉，帝國官署在北高盧只剩索瓦松一帶還能照章徵稅、任命官員、鑄造錢幣，西亞格里烏斯正是在這個殘餘上維持著羅馬的名號。克洛維斯一方則需要一條向西北擴張的通道，並取得索瓦松盆地這樣足以養活部眾的良田。薩利安法典中反覆出現的「Suessionum」與「civis Romanus」字樣，說明戰爭之前兩套法律與產權已在這一帶互相嵌套。直接導火線通常被說成索瓦松方面拒絕了法蘭克人的某些要求，或是爭奪瓦茲河與馬恩河上游的渡口與榷稅權；具體經過沒有留下可靠記載，格里高利只說雙方在索瓦松附近列陣，隨即開戰。
causeEn: The immediate cause of the Battle of Soissons was a struggle for survival between the last Roman-style regime in northern Gaul and the Frankish confederation. The background goes back to the collapse of the empire in the late fourth century: in 406 large bodies of Franks and other Germanic peoples crossed the Rhine into Gaul; in 405 the Roman general Stilicho granted the Franks a tract of land in what is now Belgium under the name of a 'rent of land', making them allies who would guard the frontier for the empire and binding them not to raid beyond it. That arrangement held for decades, but Roman power in northern Gaul grew steadily more hollow, the base of taxation and recruitment was cut away piece by piece by the tribal confederations, and by the mid-fifth century the imperial administration in the north of Gaul could still levy taxes, appoint officials and strike coin only around Soissons. Syagrius was the man who kept the name of Rome alive on top of that remnant. On the other side, Clovis needed a corridor for expansion to the north-west and a stretch of good land such as the Soissonnais basin capable of feeding his people. The repeated references to 'Suessionum' and to the 'civis Romanus' in the Salic law show that before the war two systems of law and property were already entangled there. The immediate spark is usually given as a refusal by Soissons to certain Frankish demands, or as a quarrel over the fords and the tolls on the upper Oise and Marne; no reliable account of the course of events survives, and Gregory says only that the two sides drew up in array near Soissons and the fighting began.
impact: 蘇瓦松之戰的直接後果是索瓦松王國的滅亡。這場勝利讓克洛維斯一舉取得北高盧的核心地盤：索瓦松盆地、瓦茲河流域與通往巴黎的門戶，隨後數年他逐步接收雷米、凡爾登、圖爾與安茹一帶，把原本由羅馬官府管理的稅收與兵源收編為法蘭克王室的資源。從此高盧北部不再有以羅馬人自居的政權，殘存的羅馬式機構要麼消失，要麼改以法蘭克臣屬的形式存在。更長期的後果是法蘭克王權的合法化。克洛維斯在戰後取得索瓦松的國庫、王室象徵與一批羅馬顯貴的支持者，得以自居高盧唯一的主人，並在數年後西進阿基坦、於普瓦捷擊敗西哥特殘部，把高盧大部分收入納入王國；491至511年間四子瓜分王國，則為墨洛溫王朝的分裂埋下伏線，最終演成法蘭克王國與教會同盟的體制，也構成加洛林王朝的制度基礎。在記憶與詮釋層面，索瓦松是「日耳曼人終結西羅馬」敘事的關鍵節點之一，但必須保留懷疑：現存主要文本出自六世紀教會史家之手，並非戰時記錄，他對「最後的羅馬人」之死的敘述帶有鮮明的基督教王權觀。學界至今仍爭論西亞格里烏斯的政權算不算羅馬國家、法蘭克接管算不算征服；也有研究者強調，索瓦松盆地一帶的城市、稅制與教會結構在戰後並未立刻被摧毀，而是被吸收進法蘭克統治，成為日後法蘭克王國得以延續西羅馬行政資源的關鍵。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the Battle of Soissons was the end of the Kingdom of Soissons. The victory gave Clovis the core of northern Gaul in a single stroke: the Soissonnais basin, the valley of the Oise and the approaches to Paris, and in the years that followed he absorbed Reims, Verdun, Tours and Anjou, turning revenues and manpower previously administered by Roman officials into resources of the Frankish crown. From then on no regime in northern Gaul claimed to be Roman; such Roman institutions as survived either disappeared or continued as dependencies of the Franks. The longer-term consequence was the legitimisation of Frankish kingship. After the battle Clovis had the treasury of Soissons, its regalia and the backing of a body of Roman aristocrats at his disposal, allowing him to present himself as the sole master of Gaul; a few years later he pressed west into Aquitaine and defeated the Visigothic remnant at Vouillé, drawing most of Gaul's income into the kingdom. The division of the realm among his four sons between 491 and 511 planted the seed of the partitions that shaped the Merovingian monarchy, which in turn produced the Frankish kingdom's alliance with the church and the institutional base of the Carolingian dynasty. At the level of memory and interpretation, Soissons is one of the pivotal scenes in the narrative of the Germans ending the western Roman empire, but the point must be made with caution. The main surviving text is by a sixth-century ecclesiastical historian, not a wartime witness, and his account of the death of the 'last of the Romans' carries a strongly Christian view of kingship. Scholars still argue over whether Syagrius' polity was a Roman state and whether the Frankish takeover amounted to a conquest; others stress that the towns, tax system and church structures of the Soissonnais were not destroyed overnight but absorbed into Frankish rule, which is why the Frankish kingdom was later able to inherit and reuse the administrative resources of the western empire.
result: 索瓦松之戰以法蘭克的完勝告終。西亞格里烏斯的軍隊在城外被擊潰，以羅馬人自居的政權隨之瓦解；格里高利記他被斬首，其家人則或遭處置，或退隱修院，抄本之間細節有出入。索瓦松城改由法蘭克接管，這座城既是北高盧的要塞，也是通往巴黎與塞納河谷的關鍵，因此克洛維斯把它當作下一步的跳板，而非一次性的掠奪目標。戰利品的分配也留下象徵性的一幕：格里高利記載，士兵們分配戰利品時，一名士兵看見灌木上的金色荊棘冠，替克洛維斯戴上並高呼「萬歲王」；克洛維斯接受了，從此戴荊棘冠而不戴金冠，直到他去世。這個細節說明克洛維斯的權力來自部族與戰團的直接認可，而非任何羅馬皇帝的冊封；索瓦松的冠冕、金庫與羅馬貴族的支持，只是讓這種認可更像王權。格里高利另記，索瓦松居民表示願以薩利安法典受治，克洛維斯的回答則是不接受羅馬法與異教風俗。最終結果是：北高盧從此脫離以羅馬人自居的政體，進入克洛維斯的統治；索瓦松的城牆、稅制與教會網絡被法蘭克王權接手，成為後來法蘭克王國的骨架。戰役確切的日期、地點與參戰兵力至今無法確定，戰場只能大致劃在索瓦松城外的平原，主流說法把它繫於西元486年9月27日，格里高利則把它記作「索瓦松附近瓦迪斯科斯的田地」。
resultEn: The Battle of Soissons ended in a complete Frankish victory. Syagrius' army was broken in the field outside the town and the Roman-style polity collapsed with it; Gregory records that he was beheaded, while his family was either executed or withdrew to a monastery, with the details varying between manuscripts. Soissons passed to Frankish control, and since the city was both the fortress of northern Gaul and the key to Paris and the Seine valley, Clovis treated it as the springboard for his next moves rather than as a prize to be plundered and abandoned. The sharing out of the spoils left a symbolic moment: Gregory writes that as the soldiers divided the booty, one of them saw a golden crown of thorns on a bush, set it on Clovis' head and shouted 'long live the king'; Clovis accepted it and wore the thorn crown instead of a golden one until his death. The detail shows that Clovis' authority rested on the direct acclamation of the clans and of his war-band rather than on any grant from a Roman emperor; the crown, treasury and Roman supporters of Soissons merely made that acclamation look more like kingship. Gregory also records that the people of Soissons offered to be ruled by the Salic law, and that Clovis replied that he would take neither Roman law nor pagan custom. The end result was this: northern Gaul left behind the last polity that called itself Roman and came under Clovis' rule, and the walls, taxation and church network of Soissons were taken over by the Frankish crown to form the skeleton of the later Frankish kingdom. The exact date, place and numbers of the battle remain undetermined; the field can only be roughly placed on the plains outside the town, the usual dating is 27 September AD 486, and Gregory locates the engagement at 'the field of Vadiscus near Soissons'.
